The retrieved document adds that the purported 'Flora and Fauna Act' is a persistent myth, with Aboriginal Australians never classified as fauna under such legislation. The reasoner, working from memory, recalls that before the 1960s, the legal status was defined by constitutional provisions such as Section 127 (excluding them from population counts) and Section 51(xxvi) (limiting federal laws), as well as state-level Aboriginal Protection Acts that controlled many aspects of their lives, with state laws gradually repealed or reformed over the 20th century; this recollection draws on broad public knowledge that is well-established, so it settles the question of what those main laws were.
